shape.description: Hollow square block on four corner legs, with a low arch in all four faces. The top is an open half-round cup running straight through along x, between two raised rails with small pegs. Each open cup end has a low rectangular tab loop below it, notched at the top. Underside is hollow with the cup shell visible.
shape.sizeBasis: Scale is estimated, not measured: one cell = one block width (top-down maps, trex_plans_27). A cell of about 45 mm is judged from hand and laptop-key size in IMG_0960/0963, +-5 mm. No ruler was in any photo.

evidence.shows: round side hole sits exactly at a joint: arch of upper block over cup end of lower block; red T-08 plugs in there
arch on the cup-end face and on the rail face, so arches are on all four faces
block profile: body about square, rail 0.17 slot, tab at 0.45-0.70 of height, arch 0.33 slot
T-06 between two B-01 tops at equal height 3, level
T-02, T-04 and T-06 chain through blue tops; T-06 rails level
T-03 ends on B-01 cup end
T-17 sits on the cup end, small peg through its slot

assumptions: Axes: +x = E, +y = S, z up; z is in slots above this block's own feet. Marble seat in a cup is z=0.68.

Joint rule: a block body is about a cube; pitch is 1 slot; rails stand 0.17 slot higher and nest inside the block above. Each face has a low arch, as tall as the cup is deep (0.33 slot). So the arch of an upper block plus the cup end of the lower block make a round hole at the joint, about 0.65 slot across. The cup-end port and the side round hole are the SAME port: it is a notch when the stack ends there and a hole when a block sits on top. Height is the same either way, n-0.32 slots for the nth block.

Height finding: equal-height ports give a truly level track. Side elevations on trex_plans_02 draw T-06 horizontal, and iso rails on T-06 match the floor axis (0.66-0.69 vs 0.68-0.70 rise/run, read by eye, so a slope under about 0.1 slot per cell cannot be excluded). No built-in slope was found in blocks or straights. A marble crosses level runs on speed from an earlier drop, launcher or lift. It will not start from rest there.

Scale is estimated, not measured: one cell = one block width (top-down maps, trex_plans_27). A cell of about 45 mm is judged from hand and laptop-key size in IMG_0960/0963, +-5 mm. No ruler was in any photo.
